summary: Datadog HTTP logs ingest: per-tenant key rotation failing, causing 401/duplicate events and missing deduplication
description: Issue summary: Customer FinLedger reported intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses and a burst of duplicate events in their Datadog HTTP Logs intake after performing a scheduled API key rotation. Impact: Duplicate billing concerns and noisy alerts in Datadog, potential GDPR PII leakage risk during replay windows. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod (us-east-1). Customer expects per-tenant rotating keys to apply without interruption to active webhook delivery and wants confirmation of at-most-once delivery semantics and a sample replay-proof payload. Request: provide root cause analysis, immediate mitigation, configuration change to ensure rotation applies atomically, sample payloads showing idempotency headers, and a short evidence package they can forward to their security/compliance team.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer rotated tenant API key via Console > Security > Tenant Keys. 2) Backend webhook proxy started sending logs to Datadog using new key but some proxy instances used old key due to stale tag on config rollout. 3) Datadog returned 401 for the old-key requests; client retried and eventually succeeded with new-key requests, creating duplicates because retry policy retried without idempotency token. 4) Customer observed 401 spikes starting 2024-10-28T03:12Z and duplicates clustered at 03:20-03:45Z.

investigation_notes: - Replicated rotation flow in staging by rotating tenant key and observing rollout. Found 3 of 15 webhook-proxy instances retained old config because of mismatched k8s label key. - Retry policy in proxy attempted immediate retries without sending event id header, causing Datadog to accept subsequent identical events as new. - Datadog HTTP intake provides no server-side deduplication unless client provides a unique identifier per event. - Root cause chain: human-triggered rotation -> config rollout selector mismatch -> stale proxies -> 401 responses -> immediate retry logic without idempotency header -> duplicates in Datadog.
resolution: 1) Emergency mitigation: deployed v1.3.4 to webhook-proxy that accepts old+new keys for 5 minutes post-rotation, and injects X-Redwood-Event-Id header into all outbound log POSTs when absent. 2) Updated rotation workflow in Console to perform a rolling key swap with an automated 5-minute dual-key acceptance window. 3) Added idempotency support: clients now include X-Redwood-Event-Id and we log event hashes for 48 hours for dedup checks. 4) Fixed label mismatch in k8s deployment and added a pre-rotation validation check that verifies all proxy replicas have correct labels. 5) Provided FinLedger: (a) sample payload with X-Redwood-Event-Id and dedup instructions, (b) evidence bundle (signed delivery manifest, sample headers, timeline), and (c) Confluence runbook for compliance. 6) Created follow-up internal work items for GA feature: permanent dedup index and per-tenant replayproof manifest.

customer_message: We have reviewed the evidence bundle and the duplicates stopped after your patch. We need a short note to share with our compliance team summarizing the fix and confirming that retained logs during rotation are available for audit. Please include the exact time window when dual-key acceptance was active.
closing_notes: Dual-key window for FinLedger rotation executed at 2024-10-28T03:12:00Z - 2024-10-28T03:17:00Z. Provided signed manifest and sample headers. Customer confirmed receipt on 2024-11-01. Ticket closed after confirmation and internal follow-ups created.
public_facing_summary: Resolved: Per-tenant Datadog HTTP ingest experienced duplicates during API key rotation. Fixes include a short dual-key acceptance window, idempotency headers (X-Redwood-Event-Id), and pre-rotation validation to prevent stale proxies. Evidence bundle and replay-proof sample payload delivered to customer.
